text:
The current stable version of the **Pest PHP testing framework is Pest 5**, with the latest identified patch release being **v5.3.0** [1][2]. This major iteration represents a significant advancement for PHP developers and AI agents, introducing a suite of powerful features and requiring modern PHP environments [3][4].

Pest 5 was officially launched on **July 28, 2026**, though some sources indicate a release date of July 29 or 30, 2026 [1][5]. It mandates **PHP 8.4 or higher** and is built upon **PHPUnit 13**, leveraging the latest improvements from both platforms [6][4]. Key enhancements in Pest 5 include the **Tia Engine** for Test Impact Analysis, which intelligently re-runs only affected tests to drastically reduce execution time, and new plugins for **AI evaluations** (Evals) and **agent verification** [3][4]. These features aim to streamline development workflows, improve AI agent reliability, and enhance overall testing efficiency [4].

The most recent patch release within the Pest 5 series is **v5.3.0**, which introduced a `--trace` feature for browser testing and improved baseline reuse for CI merge commits [2]. Pest 5's focus on performance, AI integration, and developer experience solidifies its position as a cutting-edge testing solution for the PHP ecosystem.

sources.title: Releases · pestphp/pest · GitHub
claims: v5.3.0 includes a --trace feature for the browser and reuses baselines across replacement CI merge commits.
v5.2.1 fixes an issue where the command `gh` was not found on Windows.
v5.2.0 adds GitLab CI baseline support, fixes issues with datasets and the `gh` command on Windows, and persists state on detached HEAD.
v5.1.4 fixes suppressing PHPUnit XML coverage during recording, keys Tia worker partials per process, and includes rector fixes.
v5.1.3 drops the bundled Boost pest-testing skill and re-anchors after a full suite run without a coverage driver.

v5.1.2 fixes treating a test skipped from a hook as finished, includes the PHP minor version in the fingerprint, addresses named dataset arguments, exit codes with --shard and --parallel, and prevents memory exhaustion when generating --tia graphs with PCOV.
v5.1.0 uses phpunit:13.3, inherits its features, and fixes livewire sfc and mutate plugin with --tia.
v5.0.4 fixes various bugs on the --tia engine.
v5.0.3 fixes datasets key incorrect in --tia mode.
v4.7.8 fixes named datasets with a single argument.

sources.title: Pest | The elegant testing framework for PHP developers and AI agents
claims: Pest is an elegant testing framework for PHP developers and AI agents.
Pest brings the joy of testing to PHP, with browser testing and AI evaluations built in.
Pest version 5 is now available.
Pest supports Test Impact Analysis (TIA) to run only affected tests.
Pest offers readable failures that explain themselves.
Pest is an all-in-one framework that includes parallel execution, coverage, mutation, and snapshots.
Pest allows running browser tests using Playwright with the same syntax as other Pest tests.
Pest enables agents to verify their own work against a live app.
Pest can be used to evaluate LLM features like code.
Pest is compatible with frameworks like Laravel, Symfony, Livewire, Inertia, WordPress, Filament, Statamic, and CodeIgniter.

sources.title: Pest 5 Now Available | Pest - The elegant PHP Testing Framework
claims: Pest 5 is the biggest version of Pest yet, built on top of PHP 8.4 and PHPUnit 13.
Pest 5 introduces the Tia Engine for Test Impact Analysis, which re-runs only tests affected by recent changes.
The Agent Plugin allows AI coding agents to verify code changes with a single command within the test suite.
The Evals plugin enables evaluation of LLM agents and AI-generated output directly from the test suite.
A first-party PHPStan plugin is available to teach PHPStan about Pest's functional API.
The Rector plugin provides automated refactoring rules to modernize test code and convert assertions.
Time-Balanced Sharding distributes tests across CI machines based on execution time for balanced completion.
Pest 5 adds new expectations including `toBeEmail()`, `toBeUlid()`, `toBeIpAddress()`, `toBeMacAddress()`, `toBeHostname()`, `toBeDomain()`, `toBeBase64()`, and `toBeHexadecimal()`.

sources.title: Installation | Pest - The elegant PHP Testing Framework
claims: Pest requires PHP 8.4+ to run.
To install Pest, first require it as a "dev" dependency using `composer require pestphp/pest --dev --with-all-dependencies`.
After installing Pest as a dependency, initialize it in your project by running `./vendor/bin/pest --init`.
To run Pest tests, execute the `./vendor/bin/pest` command.
The `pest-plugin-browser` package can be installed for browser testing in Pest.
The `pest-plugin-drift` package can be used to convert PHPUnit tests to Pest.
